analysis.title: Match Group (MTCH) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Tinder DAUs Inflect Positive; Forward Focus Anchored on Durable User & Revenue Growth
key_insights: Match Group reported Q3'26 Adj. EBITDA of $344mm, ahead of GS ($333mm) and consensus ($332mm) and above the $330-335mm guide. Adj. EBITDA margin was 38.7% vs GS 37.4%.
Tinder DAUs returned to positive YoY growth for the first time in 3.5 years, which GS attributes to the Revitalize phase of the Tinder turnaround (product roadmap, improved recommendations).
Management expects testing of real-time adaptive recommendations at Tinder to begin in Q4 and cited positive adoption of the 'Better with Friends' initiatives.

Hinge payer growth accelerated to +23% YoY in Q3 from +17% in Q2. Management reiterated confidence in $1bn of Hinge revenue in 2027, with about 1.5mm MAUs in India and Japan flagged as a 2027 opportunity.

Hinge RPP of $31.81 missed GS ($33.86) and consensus ($34.90) because of payer optimization. Management expects lower RPP YoY growth in Q4 as optimization continues and a lower-priced tier is expected to launch.
Management gave a qualitative framework in which Evergreen & Emerging (E&E) topline growth keeps declining in 2027 as the company focuses on fewer brands.
Marketing intensity is expected to stay elevated in Q4'26, ahead of prior GS expectations, partly because spend shifted from Q3 to Q4.
GS cut Q4'26 Adj. EBITDA to $330mm from $340mm (margin 38.0% from 39.2%) and FY27 Adj. EBITDA to $1.35bn from $1.42bn (margin 38.1% from 39.7%).
GS raised FY27 Tinder direct revenue to $1.87bn from $1.79bn and cut FY27 total revenue to $3.53bn from $3.58bn.

Capital returned YTD is $472mm through dividends and buybacks. GS expects continued shareholder returns to be one of three investor debates, alongside Tinder trends and operating margins versus the 2024 investor day targets.

GS maintains Buy and raises its 12-month price target to $47 from $46, equal-weighting an 11.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA multiple on NTM+1 and a DCF on 18.0x EV/FCF-SBC. The stock closed at $42.07 on Nov 2, implying 11.7% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Buy maintained and PT raised to $47 from $46 after Q3'26 EBITDA beat and Tinder DAU inflection. FY27 estimates were cut on higher marketing spend and lower Hinge RPP.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported total revenue $891mm vs GS $890mm and consensus $892mm, within the $885-895mm guide.
Q3'26 reported Adj. EBITDA $344mm vs GS $333mm and consensus $332mm (guide $330-335mm). EPS $0.73 reported vs GS $0.72 and consensus $0.71.
Q3'26 reported Tinder revenue $480mm vs GS $473mm and consensus $466mm. Tinder payers 8,879 vs GS 8,934 and consensus 8,782. Tinder RPP $18.02 vs GS $17.66 and consensus $17.70.
Q3'26 reported Hinge revenue $221mm vs GS $223mm and consensus $224mm. Hinge payers 2,312 vs GS 2,191 and consensus 2,135. Hinge RPP $31.81 vs GS $33.86 and consensus $34.90.
GS estimate: Q4'26E total revenue $870mm (prior $867mm), Tinder direct revenue $461mm (prior $449mm), Adj. EBITDA $330mm (prior $340mm), EPS $0.72 (prior $0.73).
GS estimate: FY27E EPS $2.96 (prior $3.11), FY28E EPS $3.33 (prior $3.36), FY29E EPS $3.60 (prior $3.55).
GS estimate: FY27E Hinge revenue $973mm (prior $1,008mm) and Hinge RPP $31.43 (prior $34.70). FY27E Tinder payers 8,721 (prior 8,618).
risk_factors: Increased regulatory scrutiny, including privacy laws.
Heightened competition and decreased user retention.
Security breaches and app store fees.
